transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

When I’m not on an actual call, I just can’t keep my attention on training, reports, or manuals long enough to get through them properly. I do fine during the high-intensity emergencies, but trying to sit down and focus on the paperwork or studying lately has been nearly impossible.

Have problems with attention and staying organized been present since childhood or school years, or did they start more recently during a stressful period? Also, do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different things even when there isn’t an emergency?

Honestly, looking back, this goes all the way back to elementary school where teachers were always moving my seat and I'd constantly forget to turn in my homework. These issues just really came to a head and became impossible to ignore about a year and a half ago when I started my captaincy coursework. As for worrying, no, I don't really experience constant or excessive worry about things.

Do these attention and organization problems happen in more than one part of your life, like at home, work, and in relationships, or mainly just during coursework and paperwork? Can you give one or two examples?

They definitely spill over into my home life and relationships. For instance, I'm constantly forgetting to call my wife back or letting bills sit unpaid on the counter because once they're out of sight, they're out of mind. I also can't even sit still to watch a movie with my son without constantly getting up or fiddling with my phone.

Do these attention and restlessness problems cause clear problems in your life, like poor performance reviews, missed deadlines, accidents, or conflict at home? What is the biggest consequence they’ve caused recently?

Yes, they've caused serious issues at work, including formal write-ups and falling behind on my promotion to captain because my officers don't trust me with detailed paperwork. The biggest consequence was recently getting a formal warning after a near-miss during a drill where I overlooked a critical checklist item. It's reached the point where they don't feel I can handle these responsibilities safely without extra oversight.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a longstanding pattern of inattention, disorganization, forgetfulness, and restlessness beginning in elementary school, occurring across work, home, and relationships, and causing clear occupational and interpersonal impairment. Symptoms are not better explained by generalized anxiety, which the patient denies. This is most consistent with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive type under ICD-10 coding provided.
